final_text:
Short answer: In the general (nonpregnant) adult NHANES population, the common PFAS measured in serum (PFOA, PFOS, PFNA, PFHxS) do not show consistent associations with thyroid function tests. Specifically:

What NHANES EP-WAS shows (fully adjusted model; meta-analyzed across 2007–2012 when the thyroid panel was measured):
- TSH (LBXTSH)
  - PFOA, PFOS, PFNA, PFHxS: No association detected (EP-WAS returned no significant results; none appear among top exposures linked to TSH).
- Total T4 (LBXTT4)
  - PFOA: β = −0.0068 (p = 0.764)
  - PFOS: β = −0.0096 (p = 0.750)
  - PFNA: β = −0.0079 (p = 0.673)
  - PFHxS: β = −0.0090 (p = 0.860)
  - Interpretation: All null; directions mixed/near zero.
- Free T4 (LBXT4F)
  - PFOA: β = +0.0085 (p = 0.670)
  - PFOS: β = −0.0010 (p = 0.969)
  - PFNA: β = −0.0326 (p = 0.284)
  - PFHxS: β = −0.0109 (p = 0.764)
  - Interpretation: All null.
- Total T3 (LBXTT3)
  - PFOA: β = +0.0164 (p = 0.772)
  - PFOS: β = −0.0282 (p = 0.494)
  - PFNA: β = −0.0155 (p = 0.353)
  - PFHxS: β = +0.0303 (p = 0.561)
  - Interpretation: All null.

Note on other PFAS: Perfluoroundecanoic acid (PFUA; less commonly discussed) shows a small inverse association with total T3 (β = −0.0705, p = 0.0076), but there were no corresponding effects on TSH or T4, and this does not survive stringent multiple-testing correction across the full EP-WAS catalog.

Bottom line: NHANES does not support a consistent thyroid-disrupting signal of the major PFAS (PFOA, PFOS, PFNA, PFHxS) in the general adult population for TSH, total T4, free T4, or total T3. Any PFAS–thyroid associations in NHANES are small, inconsistent across hormones, and do not replicate across the main PFAS commonly cited by ATSDR.
